products.name: AmnioFix Injectable / EpiFix Injectable (micronized dHACM, mdHACM)
products.ownership_history: Developed by MiMedx (Surgical Biologics subsidiary, Marietta GA). FDA Untitled Letter of 5 Sept 2013 to Surgical Biologics concluded micronized AmnioFix Injectable was more than minimally manipulated and needed a biologics license. MiMedx ran it as an IND/BLA program (RMAT designation for knee OA, 2018), then disbanded the Regenerative Medicine segment and suspended the knee OA program in Q2 2023, abandoning the BLA.
products.composition: Dehydrated human amnion/chorion membrane (PURION-processed) milled to a micronized powder and reconstituted in saline for injection (40-100 mg doses in trials).

regulatory.reference: No BLA. Studied under IND (number not public); FDA Untitled Letter 2013 (Surgical Biologics, AmnioFix Injectable); BLA effort abandoned Q2 2023 per MiMedx FY2025 10-K
on_label_indications: None. FDA treats micronized amniotic membrane injected for pain, inflammation or tendon/joint conditions as a 351 biologic requiring a BLA (2013 Untitled Letter; 2017/2020 HCT/P guidance; enforcement discretion ended 31 May 2021). MiMedx states it does not sell Section 351 products in the US.

products.challenge: The Level I plantar fasciitis RCT (Cazzell 2018) is still quoted in sales decks for other brands; MiMedx's own confirmatory Phase 3 in plantar fasciitis and its Phase 2b in knee OA both missed their primary endpoints, and MiMedx walked away from the BLA.

applications.evidence_summary: Cazzell 2018 single-blind RCT (n=145, 14 US sites): one mdHACM injection cut 3-month VAS pain 76% vs 45% for saline (p<0.0001). The confirmatory double-blind Phase 3 (NCT03414268) did not separate from saline on 90-day VAS (topline 13 Sept 2021) and MiMedx dropped the plantar fasciitis BLA. A 2026 meta-analysis of placental injectables in plantar fasciitis (6 studies, 324 patients) rated certainty low to very low.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; the positive trial was single-blind with a 3-month primary endpoint; the larger double-blind trial was negative and is unpublished as a paper. Achilles Phase 3 (NCT03414255, n=146) completed 2021 with no results posted. Only a 32-patient retrospective Achilles series is published.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2b RCT (NCT03485157, 446 randomized, KL 1-3) missed both primary endpoints (VAS and WOMAC at 90 days); only a pre-interim subgroup separated. A second Phase 2b (NCT05796765) was stopped by the sponsor at n=43 and the program was suspended in 2023. The only published knee data are a 100-knee retrospective series written with MiMedx employees.
applications.caveats: Negative primary endpoints; subgroup signal is post hoc; no BLA.

evidence.title: Randomized Controlled Trial of Micronized Dehydrated Human Amnion/Chorion Membrane (dHACM) Injection Compared to Placebo for the Treatment of Plantar Fasciitis
evidence.finding: Single-blind, 14 sites: 3-month VAS fell 76% with mdHACM vs 45% with saline (p<0.0001); FFI-R 60% vs 40%; no related serious adverse events.

evidence.title: Prospective, randomized, blinded, comparative study of injectable micronized dehydrated amniotic/chorionic membrane allograft for plantar fasciitis--a feasibility study
evidence.finding: Single-centre, 3 arms (saline, 0.5 cc, 1.25 cc): AOFAS hindfoot scores improved more with mdHACM at 1 and 8 weeks; 8-week follow-up only.

evidence.title: Micronized dHACM Injectable for the Treatment of Plantar Fasciitis (Phase 3)
evidence.finding: Double-blind, saline-controlled; MiMedx reported 13 Sept 2021 that it did not meet the 90-day VAS primary endpoint and that it would not file a BLA for plantar fasciitis (company release said 277 enrolled; registry lists 208).

evidence.title: Micronized dHACM Injectable for the Treatment of Achilles Tendonitis (Phase 3)
evidence.finding: Completed March 2021; no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and no publication located.

evidence.title: Micronized Dehydrated Human Amnion/Chorion Membrane Injection in the Treatment of Chronic Achilles Tendinitis
evidence.finding: Single-physician retrospective series; 66% reported symptom resolution within 45 days; no control group; MiMedx-affiliated authors.

evidence.title: Micronized dHACM vs. Saline in the Treatment of Osteoarthritis of the Knee (Phase 2b)
evidence.finding: Did not meet either primary endpoint (VAS, WOMAC at 90 days); results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; pre-interim cohort showed WOMAC separation.

evidence.title: Phase 2B Micronized DHACM vs. Saline in the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Terminated: 'Study discontinued early by Sponsor' after MiMedx suspended the program in 2023.

evidence.title: Micronized Dehydrated Human Amnion Chorion Membrane Injection in the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis-A Large Retrospective Case Series
evidence.finding: 100 knees (82 patients) given 100 mg mdHACM, KOOS followed 6 months; uncontrolled; MiMedx employees among authors.

evidence.title: Placental-derived injectable products for chronic plantar fasciitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Six studies: placebo-controlled RCTs favored placental injections (MD 3.37 points on 0-10 pain, I2=92%); GRADE certainty low to very low.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None: program disbanded Q2 2023; MiMedx FY2025 10-K records abandonment of the BLA.

bd.reimbursement: Q4145 ('Epifix, inj, 1mg') still exists in HCPCS, but the product cannot be lawfully promoted for joint or tendon injection without a BLA; any current billing of an amniotic injectable for musculoskeletal pain is a compliance red flag (see Celularity's 2022 False Claims Act civil investigative demand on injectable birth-tissue billing).
bd.notes: Useful as the cautionary tale: the best-funded amniotic injectable program in the US ended without a BLA.

products.name: AmnioFix (dHACM sheet) and AmnioCord (dehydrated umbilical cord)
products.ownership_history: MiMedx Group (Marietta, GA); AmnioFix sold since about 2011 (sheet). AmnioCord is the surgical umbilical-cord sheet sold alongside it.
products.composition: Dehydrated, PURION-processed human amnion/chorion membrane sheet (AmnioFix); dehydrated umbilical cord sheet (AmnioCord). Room-temperature storage, five-year shelf life per MiMedx.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)
on_label_indications: Homologous use as a barrier, covering or wrap at a surgical site (FDA's 2017/2020 guidance: sheet amniotic membrane used as a barrier or covering is generally a 361 HCT/P). MiMedx positions its Surgical line for 'lower extremity repair, plastic and reconstructive surgery, vascular procedures, and multiple orthopedic repairs'.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a tendon wrap or adhesion barrier in Achilles, peroneal and flexor repairs; no comparative study of AmnioFix in tendon repair located (PubMed search 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: On-label only as a barrier/wrap; any claim that it speeds tendon healing is a non-homologous claim FDA has cited in other firms' warning letters (BioXtek 2025, Celularity 2025).

applications.evidence_summary: MiMedx ran a 25-patient randomized trial of its dehydrated umbilical cord patch in open supraspinatus repair (NCT03084068, completed 2019); no results posted or published.
applications.caveats: Barrier use only; not a structural augmentation patch.

applications.evidence_summary: Adjacent use as an epidural/dural barrier, not a fusion biologic: Subach 2015 (n=5 TLIF re-explorations) reported easily detachable epidural tissue; a 143-patient randomized lumbar decompression/microdiscectomy trial (NCT02300909) completed 2018 with no results posted.
applications.caveats: Tiny case series; the randomized trial is unpublished; does not contribute to fusion.
applications.challenge: Pair to fusion only as an anti-adhesion barrier; it has no osteogenic role.

evidence.title: The use of a dehydrated amnion/chorion membrane allograft in patients who subsequently undergo reexploration after posterior lumbar instrumentation
evidence.finding: In 5 TLIF patients re-explored later, epidural tissue was easily detached where dHACM had been placed; no complications.

evidence.title: Randomized, single blind, controlled trial of dHACM in lumbar decompression and microdiscectomy surgery
evidence.finding: Completed June 2018 (primary outcome ODI); no results posted or published.

evidence.title: Prospective RCT for rotator cuff repair using a human dehydrated umbilical cord patch
evidence.finding: Completed January 2019 (ASES at 12 months); no results posted or published.

evidence.title: Dehydrated human amnion/chorion membrane use in emergent craniectomies shows minimal dural adhesions
evidence.finding: Reported minimal dural adhesions at cranioplasty after dHACM placement; MiMedx-affiliated authors.

bd.reimbursement: No Q-code located for AmnioFix (HCPCS lookup 2026-10-23); in the OR it is bundled into the DRG/APC and facilities may report C1762.
bd.notes: MiMedx Surgical category net sales $142.3M in 2025 (+20.7%), driven by AmnioFix, AMNIOEFFECT and HELIOGEN (a 510(k) bovine collagen product) per the FY2025 10-K.

products.name: EpiFix (dHACM) and EpiCord (dehydrated umbilical cord) wound allografts
products.ownership_history: MiMedx Group; EpiFix is MiMedx's lead wound product (also approved in Japan).
products.composition: Dehydrated PURION-processed amnion/chorion membrane (EpiFix) and dehydrated umbilical cord (EpiCord, EpiCord Expandable) sheets for external wound cover.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)
on_label_indications: Homologous use as a protective barrier/wound covering for chronic and acute wounds (DFU, VLU); marketed for external use

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a wound cover over the soft-tissue defect after debridement in podiatry; the DFU RCTs (e.g., Tettelbach 2019, n=110, more 12-week closures with weekly dHACM) studied chronic ulcers, not post-osteomyelitis bone cavities, and no study of EpiFix as a dead-space adjunct after bone resection was located (PubMed 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: A sheet cover does not manage bone dead space or deliver antibiotic; the one RCT in DFUs with controlled osteomyelitis (a different product, BioTissue TTAX01/Neox 1K) found no benefit over standard care.
applications.challenge: Do not present a skin substitute as an osteomyelitis therapy.

evidence.title: A confirmatory study on the efficacy of dehydrated human amnion/chorion membrane dHACM allograft in the management of diabetic foot ulcers: A prospective, multicentre, randomised, controlled study of 110 patients from 14 wound clinics
evidence.finding: Weekly dHACM plus standard care healed significantly more DFUs at 12 weeks than standard care alone (ITT and per-protocol).

bd.reimbursement: Medicare: HCPCS Q-code 'Q4186 EpiFix per sq cm; Q4187 EpiCord per sq cm (Q4131 retired)'. From 1 Jan 2026 the CY2026 PFS (CMS-1832-F, 31 Oct 2025) and OPPS rules pay non-BLA skin substitutes as incident-to supplies at one flat rate (CMS fact sheet: approximately $127.28 per cm2; MiMedx and Organogenesis 10-Ks state $127.14 per cm2), before geographic adjustment, grouped by FDA pathway (361 HCT/P, PMA, 510(k)). The MAC skin-substitute LCDs that would have cut covered products were withdrawn 24 Dec 2025; L35041 (Novitas), L36377 (First Coast) and L36690 (CGS) remain. In inpatient or OR use the graft is bundled into the DRG/APC (facilities often report C1762 connective tissue).
bd.notes: Skin-substitute spending under Medicare Part B rose to over $10B in 2024 (CMS); OIG's Sept 2025 data snapshot (OEI-BL-24-00420) flagged the surge and billing red flags. EpiFix and EpiCord were among the 18 products the withdrawn 2026 LCDs would have kept covered.

products.name: AXIOFILL (placental particulate)
products.ownership_history: MiMedx; launched about 2021 as a particulate successor to its earlier placental particulate (AmnioFill). FDA issued a Warning Letter on 21 Dec 2023 after inspections; RFD determination March 2024 that it is not a 361 HCT/P; MiMedx sued in N.D. Georgia and keeps selling it while the case runs.
products.composition: Human placental-derived particulate (MiMedx calls it a particulate wound dressing) for deep wound defects.

regulatory.reference: Contested. MiMedx markets it as a 361 HCT/P; FDA Warning Letter 21 Dec 2023 and a March 2024 Request-for-Designation decision that it does not meet Section 361 criteria (FDA treats it as Section 351). Litigation pending (N.D. Ga.).
on_label_indications: MiMedx positioning: 'replacement or supplementation of damaged or inadequate integumental tissue'. FDA has determined it is not a 361 product, so no lawful 361 indication is settled.

products.challenge: A hiring manager will ask which particulate placental products FDA has already called 351: AXIOFILL (MiMedx), Interfyl (Celularity) and PalinGen Flow (Amnio Technology) are the named examples; StimLabs and BioTissue moved their particulates to 510(k).

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for deep integumental defects; no published study of AXIOFILL in post-debridement diabetic-foot or osteomyelitis cavities located (PubMed 2026-10-23).
applications.caveats: FDA classification dispute; not a bone void filler; no antibiotic delivery.

bd.reimbursement: No Q-code located for AXIOFILL (HCPCS lookup 2026-10-23); surgical use bundled.
bd.notes: The litigation outcome will set precedent for particulate placental products.

evidence.title: Two doses of lyophilized amniotic fluid vs saline placebo in knee osteoarthritis
evidence.finding: Completed April 2018; no results posted.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)

products.name: AmnioBand (Membrane, Guardian, Particulate)
products.ownership_history: MTF Biologics (Edison, NJ), non-profit tissue bank.
products.composition: Aseptically processed dehydrated human amnion-chorion membrane (dHACA); particulate form billed per mg.

regulatory.reference: none (361 HCT/P; establishment registered with CBER)
on_label_indications: Homologous use as a wound covering/barrier (sheet). The particulate form's status was not confirmed from a primary source.

evidence.title: Aseptically Processed Placental Membrane Improves Healing of Diabetic Foot Ulcerations: Prospective, Randomized Clinical Trial
evidence.finding: 85% vs 25% healed at 12 weeks; mean 3.8 grafts per healed wound; tissue cost about $1,400 per healed DFU.

bd.reimbursement: Medicare: HCPCS Q-code 'Q4169 Artacent Wound; Q4189 Artacent AC 1 mg; Q4190 Artacent AC per sq cm; Q4216 Artacent Cord; Q4336-Q4339 newer variants'. From 1 Jan 2026 the CY2026 PFS (CMS-1832-F, 31 Oct 2025) and OPPS rules pay non-BLA skin substitutes as incident-to supplies at one flat rate (CMS fact sheet: approximately $127.28 per cm2; MiMedx and Organogenesis 10-Ks state $127.14 per cm2), before geographic adjustment, grouped by FDA pathway (361 HCT/P, PMA, 510(k)). The MAC skin-substitute LCDs that would have cut covered products were withdrawn 24 Dec 2025; L35041 (Novitas), L36377 (First Coast) and L36690 (CGS) remain. In inpatient or OR use the graft is bundled into the DRG/APC (facilities often report C1762 connective tissue).
